title: An allele-frequency puzzle
hook: Predict the genotype mix from allele frequencies.

knows: A and a are two alleles and their frequencies sum to one.
doesNotKnow: How allele frequencies determine expected genotype frequencies in the stated ideal model.

misconception: Allele frequency equals the frequency of its homozygous genotype.
objective: Calculate or interpret genotype frequencies under Hardy–Weinberg assumptions.

claims.text: Question, chart and reveal: In a large randomly mating population under Hardy–Weinberg assumptions, allele frequencies are p(A) = 0.6 and q(a) = 0.4. What percentage of individuals is expected to have genotype Aa? The model gives AA = p² = 36%, Aa = 2pq = 48% and aa = q² = 16%. The requested Aa frequency is 48%. These are ideal expectations, not a guarantee for a finite population.
claims.source: Derived from p², 2pq and q² under the stated model; OpenStax https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/19-1-population-evolution

claims.text: Bars are idealized expected frequencies, not measurements or guarantees for a finite population.
Recall: Under the two-allele Hardy–Weinberg model, which expression is the expected heterozygote frequency? The two heterozygous combinations each contribute pq, so their sum is 2pq.

recall.question: Under the two-allele Hardy–Weinberg model, which expression is the expected heterozygote frequency?
recall.why: The two heterozygous combinations each contribute pq, so their sum is 2pq.
